utterances.text: I don't know the specific roads, but I do know, since there was some journalists in Kosovo who were taken prisoner by certain KLA members at check-points, that there were roadblocks along different routes. And if one would get off a highway after two 2 or 3 hundred metres, one would encounter a barricade directing you in one particular direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that people went from Pristina to Pec via Rozaj and Kula?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with such details.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D176, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next have D003-2591 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While waiting for it, can you tell me whether you remember the date of the previous directive?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one we just saw? I think it was the 20th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a correction for the transcript. It should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, witness, which day in July was it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 29th?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, the previous one, the 28th. This is a new document. First of all, this is an order to break-up DTS forces and armed rebellion forces in Kosova and Metohija sent by the 3rd Army commander on the 29th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When a directive is issued as a strategic document, then operational strategic groups, that is to say, subordinate units of the army, further develop their own orders based on that directive. This is standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us go to chapter 4 in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- in both versions. Does this confirm what you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I did mention the other element or a stage. Reference is made of members of the former provincial Kosovo MUP who joined the KLA thus creating a parallel set of institutions or government in 1990 and 1991. They separated their part of the MUP, forming their own organs. The same happened with education. I spoke more about other organs and institutions yesterday rather than the MUP. In any case, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is mentioned here are former JNA members, then we have former members of the provincial SUP, and then political convicts, and people from earlier battle-fields in Bosnia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I referred to. I stated the names of some officers who were released from prisons by a general pardon that took place, then I also mentioned the names of those officers who were prosecuted in Zlatar, in the Zlatar Operation, and released subsequently. As well as people who fought previously in Bosnia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the last part of the sentence, we find among the terrorists, there is a number of mercenaries, first and foremost from the Islamic countries. Can you comment that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I but I only have general knowledge of that such as the one I shared with you concerning the persons who came from Bosnia or Croatia or those who used to be members of the JNA. I know them by their names. However, this piece of information is something that I only have general information about, and I have no reason to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to page 2, paragraph 1, of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you, Witness, should look at the last paragraph in the Serbian version of this page concerning weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So will I. I had no information about types of weapons, but while reading orders and reports we went through in the documents you showed me, these calibres are frequently referred to, and I mean hand-held rocket launchers, mortars. I came across many of those in the documents I viewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The information you have concerning their weapons, does this confirm what they had in 1999, or did they have any modern -- more modern systems?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was within the remit of the intelligence administration. It was not of any particular interest to me and the people I worked for. In any case, they could have only received more modern weapons by that time. This takes me back to General Lazarevic's intervention when he said that some equipment was parachuted in the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, since we are short with time, tell us immediately then what it is that is your direct knowledge, otherwise we'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 2, General, in the B/C/S. It is the third paragraph in the English.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about these forced mobilisations; do you have any information concerning that in the time you were re-activated?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing beyond what I've already told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go to the last page of this document. It is page 12 in the B/C/S. In the English, page 14. No, page 13. Sorry, this is the last page. I need the penultimate page. This is the addendum on the composition and strength of groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, am I right in saying that the 3rd Army commander at the time was Lieutenant-General Dusan Samardzic and that he issued this order?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There were five copies of this document distributed to the addressees mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these were his immediate subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore it was the command of the Pristina Corps, the Nis Corps, command of the 203rd --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mixed artillery brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about number 4?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command of the logistics base, 202nd base.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about number 5?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military district of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we didn't touch upon the topic of organisation of the Federal Defence Ministry in the territory of the FRY. How did they function territorially speaking? Were they completely independent, in an independent formation answerable only to the Secretariat for National Defence, or did they have any links to the army? I mean specifically the civil protection and civil defence.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were fully under the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D177, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D003-2645.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, is this another 3rd Army commander's order with the purpose of operationalising the directive that we saw?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here pursuant to the order of the Chief of the General Staff number, date, so and so dated the 24th of July. And in the directive we had the 27th of July. But this is not contentious. There must have been an order pursuant to which this order, brief order follows -- sent through a dispatch means.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit D178, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see exhibit -- or document -- 65 ter document 04053.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 04035. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But while we are waiting for the document to appear, General, please, can the military wait for the country to be attacked to start preparing for its defence, or would it, on the basis of the information available, prepare itself to be ready when the aggression starts?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever the military does in peacetime is prepare for the possibility of an overall aggression against the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. See we have the 16th of January 1999 directive of the General Staff of the VJ. Did you have occasion earlier to see this document?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've noticed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can see, please -- Mr. Stamp, are you trying to tell me something, or? Okay then, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this directive was adopted at a time when there was a threat of activating a NATO order on the aggression against Yugoslavia? I believe that that dated from October 1998.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the date of this directive, but I see that it contains elements of a war plane because now it has a code-name GROM-3 or Thunder-3. Grom, thunder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do believe that you can see now, Witness, the date of the directive. Can you see it? I can.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that's the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 16th of January?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, January 1999 anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Judging from your experience, I would like to use that experience to take a look at an item in this directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 3 of the B/C/S version, please. At the end of Roman numeral II. This is page 2, please turn to B/C/S page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the paragraph above the Roman numeral II, the routes.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, this is a classical directive as been prepared within war plans. On the basis of all the relevant information, an assessment is made of the state of affairs on the goals and possible axis of operations and the grouping and concentration of the forces. See here the axis of expected activities and then pursuant to this a unit will be issued with orders to prepare themselves and be ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'd like to ask you, the expected NATO axis of aggression, Kacanik Gorge, and the Vrbnik axis, do you know anything about that? Do you know anything about this being mentioned in any plans?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in military geography, as taught in military schools, there are estimated axes and routes for certain operational units for strategic activities. These are known. There are no -- there is no third option. They may launch parachuters, but lands forces cannot pass anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From the moment when you were re-activated, although this was not your area of expertise, did KLA step up their activities along the axis which were expected routes of land aggression, the Kacanik Gorge and Morina and Vrnmica and Capusa [phoen] along the border?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cafa Pruse and Cafa Sani [phoen], yes. Well, the army was grouped along their axis, and the focus of the military's activities pursuant to this directive, and of course they moved along the axis where the army forces were concentrated. It would not be worth while to act and operate on hill tops where there was nobody else. They worked along the axis as advanced troops of a possible invasion or aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit D179, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document D003-3127. D003-3127. Can we turn to page 2, please, of this document. Please let's zoom in on the stamp and show it to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've seen this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this announcement recorded at the staff of the Supreme Command, the office of the Chief of General Staff, General Staff of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was registered and recorded in the office of the Chief of the General Staff; and this is the announcement drafted in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the English version as well? I would like to tender it into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the evidence to your knowledge, General, that this announcement was ever made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I see it for the first time here. I notice that the date until which the KLA should abandon their arms has been introduced. This looks as a draft of a text which later on would be finalized. And the other thing is that it's drafted in Serbian, whereas most of the population there were Albanians in Kosovo and this appeal had to be addressed to them. This seems as a conceptual draft, but I'm not sure and I'm not aware whether this was sent down to the ground. I don't know what were the channels of this announcement, maybe through the radio or over the television, but also as leaflets. But at the time leaflets could not be dropped because our air force could not -- air force aircraft could not fly over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D180, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although it's not in the proper order, but given your answer can we see document D003-2553.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is another order by the Supreme Command staff and concerns military territorial detachments; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is paragraph 5 or item 5, and please offer your comment on it.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to comment, it's very clearly stated in the text. I can read it out loud. What is being done is that units should be strengthened by persons living in Kosovo of Albanian ethnicity. This is dated 31st of March. I'm not sure what the question of yours is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, the question is the Supreme Command staff counted on Albanian population to strengthen the ranks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, I think I see Mr. Stamp's problem. It is our problem. The document on the screen doesn't contain what you are describing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm discussing paragraph 5 or item 5, but it seems we have the wrong document in English, and this is why you don't have that. I'm very sorry, I did not take heed. The B/C/S version is the correct one, but the English version is not. And you can see the English document bears the date of the 2nd April, 1999, and the Serbian the 31st of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment we can have no ready solution because this is the translation that is attached in e-court. We would have to hunt through to try and find the correct translation attached to some other document. So maybe the witness could read item 5. It can then be -- appear in translated version in the transcript, and you can ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, please read out paragraph 5 into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The military territorial detachment will be brought up to strength by the command of the military district of Pristina by the non-allocated conscripts of Albanian, of Siptar, and other ethnic background who live in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, my question is: Am I right in saying that the Supreme Command staff reckoned with the able-bodied reservists of Albanian and other ethnic affiliation in the war activities that started on the 23rd of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this order. This is the first time I see it. But what I'd like to say is that during my tour of security organs in Kosovo, I received briefs from security organs who were Albanians themselves who in the peacetime had been appointed -- selected and appointed as security officers and who had graduated from the Pancevo school. So not all of them had been excluded. However, something is strange here. The command of the military district in Pristina, as any other military district command, has a certain number of military territorial detachments. I have to ask this question: Why in March when the war had started would they issue an order for them to be included into the ranks? It would have been logical that they be included in to military territorial detachments in 1998, way before that. May I remind you that I know about the order whereby the command of the 3rd Army ordered for weapons to be distributed only to the Serbs within the ranks, so I cannot deny that there had been some obstruction dating from 1991, 1992, in terms of including Albanians into the ranks of conscripts and the others. Because objectively there were security concerns with their presence in military units because they had started terrorist attacks, thefts of military equipment, and arms; so I believe that military territorial detachments were 99 per cent Serb. I do not know about this order. I have no grounds to doubt its credibility and authenticity. It bears all the stamps, but it has had no effect. I know of detachments comprised of Albanians, Turks, and Romas, I wouldn't know about any of that. It would not be politically correct to establish such a military unit. All our units were always ethnically heterogenous. And I don't see any reasons why such an ethnically exclusive detachment would be formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but I'm not interpreting para 5 as detachments being mono-ethnic, but that they be brought up to strength with the ones who existed but who weren't organised in any units, not the formation of new ones.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this: It says to form a military territorial detachment in the war, and three territorial companies. So this means the formation of a new detachment which has a territorial companies and detachments and they have territorial platoons. And this is a new territorial detachment. Before that, the territorial detachments were already in existence in the Nis Corps, the Pristina Corps, and in every other military district as well; and it was composed of the military territorial detachments, not a territorial company. But military territorial company and military territorial platoons. So I have the impression that this was written in haste to put right something that had not been previously done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence, or rather should it just be MFI'd before we have the English translation or is it sufficient to tender the document as it stands with the interpretation received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification with a view to the correct translation being included at some time. You found the correct number, I see, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. Everything is possible when we have Ms. O'Leary here. I see it up on my screen here, and I'm sure it will come up on e-court very soon. Then I'd like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you given the correct number to the court officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's still not in e-court, but we do have the translation. Well, we can leave it MFI'd until it comes up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit D181 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, document under 65 ter 01480 next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this something you are aware of? It is preparatory order for a directive; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the date is the 9th of April, 1999; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just comment. When this is addressed personally to the Chief of Staff, then you don't have delivered to such-and-such or so-and-so that we were talking about earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. But I don't see what this Roman I is up there. What's the Roman I? Can we see top of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the abbreviation for the first administration, if I'm right. First directory to administration. Yes, that was the first one in the JNA. Perhaps I'm right, perhaps not, I don't really know. Occupations administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D182, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, the next document under 65 ter is 1481, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying, General, that this is a directive of the Supreme Command staff of the 9th of April that was announced previously. And this is copy number 1, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's interesting to note here, as far as I'm concerned, well, was this archived or not? I don't see a stamp from the military archive. And that's true of the previous documents as well. As the Supreme Command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. DT number 22-1?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's state secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, what is this 1 -- copy 1?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first copy of this document, and I suppose at the end we'll see who it was sent to, delivered to, at the end of this directive; and it was supposed to go to all operative and strategic groups, which means that there's copy number 1, 2, 3, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So is the first document where we see in the heading the copy number. I'm asking you about the left-hand side, DT number 22-1.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, I see, that says state secret. That's quite a different protocol. It's not a protocol of the Supreme Command staff. It's a separate protocol for documents relating to a war plan and state secrets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have page 2 of this document displayed, please, because I'm interested in looking at para 2.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So, General, we are dealing with a time of war; am I right in saying that what is expected is that from the territory of Macedonia, the aggressive forces have about 20.000 men, and from Albania 10.000 men; is that what this is?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those are estimations. Now, how -- what the situation was like in practice as far as I know, there were more of them in Macedonia, more troops than there were in Albania, more men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at Albania, what is the estimate there? Did your information tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was under the intelligence administration, but unless I'm wrong, there were 15.000 men before that. So it oscillated, it varied. But this is a sort of schematic that we use in compiling these documents for orientation purposes. Whether these are the exact figures, we only see later on during the action itself, so this is an estimation of those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have page 12 called up, please, of this document. It's page 12 of the English as well, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We have a stamp there of the Supreme Command staff and the signature of the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there is a stamp and there's General Ojdanic's signature there; and as I said, we see where the copies were sent to. Copy number 1, copy number 2, so everything is in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D183, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document under 65 ter is 01483.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, we are now going to see a supplement to the previous directive on the 12th of April, 1999. Am I right, is that what it is?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm moving on to another area now, and as we are coming up to the break, I would like to suggest that we take our break now and then begin with a new topic after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now to resume at 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, we managed to go through all these documents that I call combat documents, as a layperson. You went through a number of directives and orders from the Pristina Corps, the 3rd Army, and the various brigades. Did you see in any of those documents that it contains something that would be against Albanian civilian population or any other civilian population for that matter?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your active service, did you hear or have information about the army participating in any actives directed against civilian population?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Perhaps I can clarify further. In a great many documents in the item stipulating security measures and moral in the army, which would be standard items within an order, there were strict orders to subordinate units that entering premises is prohibited, that they should bear in mind that they only engage terrorists and protect civilians. Some documents also contain provisions on how and where people should be assembled in order to protect them. The treatment of any captured Siptar terrorist members is also prescribed as well as points of assembly of such prisoners and the way they should be handed over to the MUP. I think one order, military order of the Pristina Corps command, we also find that reference is made to a refugee population from an Albanian village in which there probably had been terrorist acts and they fled to the woods. In that order, the military unit is ordered to assist those civilians to return to their settlement. I think I saw 2 or 3 MUP dispatches for Kosovo. But as regards the military orders, some of them were linked to certain MUP dispatches on how and where to return that civilian population. In all of those documents, emphasis was placed on civilians being excluded from any war activities, combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As a very senior official, did you ever receive an order to the effect that you should either tolerate or implement -- that you should either tolerate or not institute procedure against people who participated in, say, arson and destruction of religious objects?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one has a right to issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I also right to say that you never issued such an order to any of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never did. First of all, I could not issue orders. And I know for certain that no trained officer would do that. First of all, there would be violating the law, and their subordinates were not expected to implement such an order. And they would have to notify their superiors about the existence of such an order. Otherwise they would be committing a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The military police was also within your domain and they have great powers in terms of prosecuting -- investigating military personnel who committed crimes. I wanted to ask you something in relation to that. Irrespective of the chain of command in terms of orders, have you ever heard of procedures not being instituted against perpetrators of crimes, and that such acts were being tolerated in any way?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, I know of only one case during the seven days of my stay in Kosovo when a crime was committed. It was the crime of murder, and certain corpses were disposed of in Gornja Klina. It was the only case that was not prosecuted. When the military police were supposed to carry on -- carry out on-site investigation, by that time the terrorists had taken up the area of Gornja Klina; and therefore, there was no investigation undertaken. But the lieutenant-colonel in whose unit the three volunteers charged with that crime had them arrested and they were eventually brought before the Nis military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on to a document. This one I believe already has its P number. Well, let's see P679.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, I wanted to show you a few documents that have to do with volunteers and their treatment. Therefore, I'd look to discuss them. As briefly as possible, can you tell us something about this document?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document during its preparation, and I also know how it was implemented. In all wars that took place in the former Yugoslavia, I conclude based on that that there is a standard procedure of how volunteers could be introduced into units, which conditions need to be met, and how they should be treated once deployed. I said that there were two assembly points for volunteers, one was in Grocka and I believe since this is an introductory order -- sorry, not Grocka, Bubanj Potak. And the other one was near Nis; I can't recall the exact centre name. In any case, given that NATO aviation targeted Bubanj Potak, the centre was moved to Grocka. This document envisaged a certain procedure in terms of receiving and checking the background of any volunteers as well as their health status and cooperation with the MUP concerning any background information on those volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this. Let's cite and example. If I were a military reservist, I have been assigned to a certain unit but never received a call to report there, could I go to Nis and introduce myself as a volunteer, would I be accepted?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could go there, but you wouldn't be taken in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see P680 next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think you saw this document as well.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, am I right in saying that the staff of the supreme corps command reacted immediately upon being notified of a problem?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was one single problem with certain volunteers. The order envisaged that they cannot stay as a group representing a separate unit. What should have taken place instead was that they be deployed among various units pertaining -- depending on their military specialties. They were supposed to fit in as reserve soldiers of the VJ. However, in some cases such as the 37th Brigade in Glogovac, some 50 or 60 of them arrived, and the commander, instead of putting them into various units, he left them as a separate unit, appointing a Stevan Jekic for commander. This was not supposed to happen, but in practice it did, and most problems came from such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But here we see that the Supreme Command staff acted as early as the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was prior to my arrival, but that practice continued later on since we kept pointing out the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And senior bodies always insisted on preventing such occurrences in subordinate commands. However, we all know what life may be like.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter document 4016. I may have gone wrong in terms of chronology in my binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, the date is the 14th of April, whereas the one before that was the 7th of April. This was the next step taken by the Supreme Command staff in terms of chronology?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous document was the most complete one since it set out the criteria. This is a document of the staff, but some reception centres did not function at all, say the one in Montenegro, since there was general obstruction on the part of Montenegro in the war effort. This is only to confirm that having learned from previous experience with volunteers not being deployed properly, that the Supreme Command staff tried to act appropriately in any following situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit D185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have D003-3032.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This document is not directly related to the previous one, but I'm interested in the issue of mobilisation, hence I find item 1 interesting. Could you please comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out item 1 of this document since I believe it is very important.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, just comment on it.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I laughed a bit, and I'll explain why. There's nothing strange in having psychologists in war units per establishment and even in some peacetime units. What is suggested here is that at the level of brigade command and higher up, such psychologists had to be employed because of the various trauma encountered in such war situations. The part that I laughed at was this, it says "platoons for psychological and propaganda activities," citing several strategic formations. Perhaps I can go back to what I was asked once, something about opera. "Opera" was shorthand for a particular body which had to do with psychological and propaganda warfare. In any case, this may not be directly related to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I believe it would be far more interesting to learn something about the opera case, but I would still like to stay with these documents. In any case, joking aside, this was a prevention measure so as to avoid any excesses due to the war trauma suffered.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not only a measure of prevention. Such platoons were also charged with counterpropaganda, they were there to oppose the enemy propaganda having their own experts from various professions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see, please, document 003-2550 but before we work on it, I move to admit this previous document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D186, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this, I think, is a general document on reporting. Could you be concise in commenting on it, I believe that you touched upon it yesterday or the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were we notified of this, Your Honour, or if you could help me to find it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend, yes for both. But the wrong document was shown on the screen. Maybe I misspoke. D003-2550 is the one that I'm seeking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document was clear. It warns of the need of regular reporting and verification of the information being reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm not sure. If this document has not been tendered, I now move to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see now, please, D003-2648.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is supposed to be a combat report by the Pristina Corps dated the 3rd of April, 1999. It is recognisable as such to you by its format?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is supposed to be a daily report sent to the operation centre; and if you noticed in the last item of the order, this was item 11, it's always stated regular daily reports should be submitted by this hour every day, and irregular reports or interview reports were never ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In peacetime, these would be daily reports and in wartime these would be combat reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D188, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another document of a similar format, D003-2585.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, is this the same format of such report, this time dated the 4th of April, 1999, sent by the Pristina Corps to the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this went through teleprinter as well. They have the same format. First item about the enemy, the second is neighbouring units, the tasks of similar units, and this is a format prescribed for all command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It too will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D189, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, D003-2633 to be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And before we see it on the screen, General, this is going to be a report one step higher from the commander of the 3rd Army to the General Staff it is a combat report dated the 13th of April, 1999. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those reports coming from army commands, different from corps level or brigade level, are far more fleshed out in terms of data and information, which is only normal because they are compiled on the basis of subordinate units, daily reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that army command reports in this case, 3rd Army's report, consolidate all the important developments in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Army based on the subordinate units reports delivered to the command of the 3rd Army during the day?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be slight differences. You said with respect to all the information submitted to -- during the day. It is not a mechanical copy paste. Information must be triaged and consolidated, but in essence all important developments and events have to be reported on for the whole of the territory and for all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now. Let me ask you, if something is not contained in a report of the commander of the 3rd Army concerning operational events or matters down there, does that mean that the Supreme Command staff will not be notified of such things?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does mean, but the Supreme Command staff has also other mechanisms which they used. And that would be to send professionals to the ground and match the reported facts with --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Yes, but this previous witness's answer was that the Supreme Command staff had other instruments meaning that they would send their own professionals on the ground to match what was being reported with the state of affairs on the ground as they find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I keep returning to the 25th of May have document by General Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is an intervention that the transcript does not reflect. Witness's answer to my question, Am I right in saying in respect of my previous question?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The content of the complaints of General Pavkovic dated the 25th of May, should they have been contained in the preceding periods, daily reports, that were submitted to the Supreme Command staff?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to be brief. They should have been, but I will most probably be in a situation to try to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see document D003-3102 [Realtime transcript read in error "D003-3012"].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is another daily report dated 29th of April, 1999, sent by the commander of the 3rd Army. Is this the prescribed format of daily reporting?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are we notified of this, Your Honour? A few documents have been coming through which we just can't find in our records.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it is not [as interpreted] D003-3102. It is reflected erroneous in the transcript. While the general is taking a look at it, Mr. Stamp, we received it in our notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, is this the same format but with a different date?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have anything on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Neither do I.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same format.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D191, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to see D003-3004, if the usher can assist us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, is the format of this document authentic? Have you had an opportunity to see it in practice?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't had an opportunity, but this is a land army sector issuing an instruction regulating in greater detail certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 4 of this document, and there is a ledger number. That page. Can we see the stamp bearing the ledger number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me first explain that the POV number differs from the others. In the others there was a strictly confidential -- there is a ledger for strictly confidential and confidential documents, and that is a protocol of the land forces sector. I see that the military post is 1122.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would start with page 4, but you see, General, we see the Chief of the General Staff Dragoljub Ojdanic signing this instruction?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in order. He would verify and approve such an instruction. And you see a corner of the Military Post 1122-1 which would be the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. This is their stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I move to enter this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see now 65 ter document 1475.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Hence we know what is written here, could we please hear your comments on items 4 and 6 briefly.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This regulated the procedure on capturing POWs in combat and how they are to be treated. In item 4, they are -- this deals with commander saboteurs, paratroopers, Special Forces operating within Yugoslavia, and it spells out that they should become prisoners of war when they are surrender, if they are wearing uniforms. This is in compliance with laws in force. And item 6 regulates the need to provide wounded and ill prisoners with adequate assistance. Now this has been highlighted and spelled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I move to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document under 65 ter is 1486, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now, it's interesting to see what he is warning them about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is about this two week period and the Supreme Command staff to the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anything lower down on the document where it says "I hereby caution ..." May we have the bottom of the document in B/C/S or the next page and in English, please. He is actually reminding them of the order he issued earlier on and says warning and says that it's urgent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D194.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told that it is a single-page document. There was a reference in the transcript to a second page, but I think it's a lower part of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. The end of the first page; the bottom of the first page. Quite right. For the time being, let it remain that way, Your Honour. I should now like -- just a moment, please. Let's move on and we'll come back to that. Now, under 65 ter document 1944 next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can confirm from what it says here with respect to international law of war, when I was re-activated, I received all these booklets regulating these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to tender this document into evidence as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D195, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document under 65 ter is 1902.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The document is in order. The same questions are highlighted and an assignment is given to the security organs and command organs that they shall collect information about these incidents and inform others about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this be tendered into evidence as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D196, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D003-2742, a Defence document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this date here, the 10th of May, and this is the administration for morale?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is for recruitment, mobilisation, and system related affairs, but we have the legal department within that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in point 1 is insistence made upon the application of international war law once again?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed and commanders and komandirs are asked to take all necessary measures to prevent violation of those principles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit D197, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is a Defence document D003-3001.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, here we have an order from the Pristina Corps command dated the 16th of April, 1999, referring to security for the civilian population; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us the basic characteristics contained in this order?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to read it first because I haven't seen it. Yes, this order is very precise. It defines everything in very precise terms, what should be done, the tasks. It's a task to the army and the MUP organs to work jointly and to inform the civilian population on time about the efforts, or rather, attacks that are to follow, whether they be NATO attacks or Siptar forces, and to give assistance for evacuation to the most suitable areas. And everything follows those general lines. And I've always mentioned that in one of the combat reports I notice that the population had taken shelter and then after the action was over, the officers tried to return them. Whereas there was a dispatch from MUP that the local population be returned to the villages. I can't remember the number of document, but it's linked to this order. And we can see on the basis of that that people did act upon the order. Now whether anybody did, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I have time for one more question; it is this: Did you ever hear that army force or police forces surrounded a village where there were no members of the KLA present in order to shell it or launch action against it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and judging by the documents that I've read, there were always, among the casualties, terrorists casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General. Your Honours, I think our time is up for today, and of course, I'd like to tender the previous document into evidence before we close. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit D198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djurdjic, what is your state of progress?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm nearing the end. I'm not at the very end, but I'm sure that Mr. Stamp and I will get through this witness tomorrow. There's no doubt about that, Your Honours. So rest assured. I have a few more documents to get through, but I think we've been through a large number of documents. I'll have another 10 to 15 minutes of documents, and then I'd like to sum up my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I hope we do better than merely concluding the evidence of this witness tomorrow, but I hope you'll both bear in mind the witness has been sitting here pummeled with documents for some very considerable length of time now; it must be very demanding and tiring. We will adjourn now to resume tomorrow at -- Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do apologise for interrupting, but the MFI D181 is now D003 -- that was a correction to the transcript -- 3200. That's the correct number for the record. And that's the English translation. The correct English translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn now to resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
